Just getting the discussion going - 15 makes sense.

After looking at options, I think using PAM gives us the cleanest way to do this rather than using /etc/profile. Open to discussion though.
Seems okay if we really only want a 5 minute timeout only on login processes and only on systems which use Bash.
Ideally the changes made here (which affect a running BMC) would also be made in libpam_%.bbappend so they affect the BMC's readonly file system, so eventually this script would not be needed.
I'm not very happy with how it was done but is there a way to do this that doesn't require a full copy of the existing login file which then has a conflict with the shadow service?
You can do the similar grep/echo in a `do_install:append()` routine for PAM.

the issue seems to be that the shadow package is what creates the login file. At least in my build, it doesn't exist at the time so the grep inside do_install:append() fails. Is there a way to enforce ordering?

Also while I am in here, since it's been 4 years since that conversion script was done, is it still needed or can I move the rest of the greps out of that service.
Done

Sorry about my delayed response.

The conversions performed by convert-pam-configs.sh [(1) s/cracklib/pwquality/, 
(2) add pwhistory conf file, (3) s/tally2/faillock/] can be removed when they are no longer needed ["when there is no longer a supported conversion path from a firmware image which uses the old style PAM modules to the new style"].  A couple of years seems long enough to leave those conversions in there.  I don't need them any more.  Other folks may have different expectations (YMMV).

TL;DR: The conversion script was only needed because the /etc/pam.d/common-* files could be written to by normal BMC operations [such as changing the number of failed password attempts vis Redfish /redfish/v1/AccountService property AccountLockoutThreshold].  Writing to these config files created a read/write overlay file which was not updated during a BMC firmware update operation, so any underlying changes to the readonly files (such as performed by the libpam recipe) would not be seen.

This specifically targets the Linux-PAM "login" service.

For context, the way this change becomes relevant is as follows: the "login" process puts up a "login:" prompt and waits for a username to be entered (typically from a TTY), and then invokes Linux-PAM as the "login" service.

Notably, logins from other vectors such as `ssh -p22 user@BMC` (accesses BMC command shell) or `ssh -p2200 user@BMC` (see github.com/openbmc/obmc-console) come to PAM as either the "dropbear" or "sshd" service, so they would not have this environment variable.
Yes - that is the point of the change.
Acknowledged
Typo: s/logi/login/
Acknowledged

This might not work for all OpenBMC images.  Some OpenBMC images have replaced the Bash shell with the BusyBox "ash" shell.  And Bash shell uses TMOUT, the Bourne shell uses TIMEOUT, and the Ash shell apparently uses ASH_IDLE_TIMEOUT.

hmm - we could set all 3 or we could let other users override?  Perhaps something like this?

TMOUT=300
# Uncomment for ash
# ASH_IDLE_TIMEOUT=300
# Uncomment for Bourne
# TIMEOUT=300
Done

Should we put this into a subdirectory like `/etc/default`? Or `profile.d`?  I don't really like new unattached files in /etc because it has the possibility of colliding and nobody really knows obviously what it is for.
I don't think profile.d makes sense since this isn't loaded by the profile service (or shouldn't be). Maybe /etc/default/pam-tty-environment?
Done
updated to resolve the circular dep issue.
Seems okay to me.  TTY logins would have a 15 minute idle timeout (changed from no timeout).  I would be happy to see this become the project's default.

In order to make it easier to override the values do we want to add a bitbake variable and a `sed` invocation here?

`DEFAULT_TTY_TIMEOUT=900`.

I don't think this phrase is needed.  If you keep it, please clarify there are three different time frames:
(1) The firmware image builder can configure the default by changing the bitbake variable in their bbappend file.
(2) The BMC administrator can change the default by editing the /etc/default/pam-login-environment file on their BMC.  This change will only take effect for sessions created after the change.
(3) The user logged into the command shell can change the value in their own shell.  That change will only take effect for that shell invocation.
cleaner without it now that its settable via var.
Looks good to me, with some suggestions.

See my comment in the bbappend file.  This would be:
TMOUT=@DEFAULT_TTY_IDLE_TIMEOUT@
...along with the other two lines.
I like this better. I was struggling since everything kind of had the same name and the @ @ makes it more obvious.
It seems clear enough the timeout value is in seconds.
I'd like to keep this one, I dont think it's harmful.

Should this use the ?= operator to set this bitbake variable's default value?  I don't know bitbake well enough to say.
Ref: https://docs.yoctoproject.org/bitbake/bitbake-user-manual/bitbake-user-manual-metadata.html#setting-a-default-value
Thanks, have not used this syntax before but seems correct from the doc.

To avoid confusion, can we make it more clear this is a build-time replacement value?  For example, various recipes use @SOME-IDENTIFIER@ to denote replacement values for pathnames.  Can we do something similar here?  For example:
1. Change this like to:
sed -i "s/@DEFAULT_TTY_IDLE_TIMEOUT@/${DEFAULT_TTY_IDLE_TIMEOUT}/" ${PAM_LOGIN_ENV}
2. Remove line 89 (TIMEOUT_STRING="DEFAULT_TTY_IDLE_TIMEOUT").
3. Make the corresponding change in pam-login-environent.
